extracted.intended_audience: poets/performers and judges participating in Ventura College 2025 Poetry Slam
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging rubric for live spoken-word/poetry-slam performances at Ventura College (2025). Covers eligibility, performance constraints, conduct expectations, scoring mechanics, tie procedures, and detailed judging criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Each solo poem must be of the poet’s own creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be original work by the performer (no co-authorship/covering others' poems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets should recite their poems from memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorization is required/preferred and is explicitly called out in both rules and judging (Performance: 'The poet has memorized their poem').

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit and overtime penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Each poet gets three minutes (plus a ten-second grace period) to read one poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the poet goes over time, points will be deducted from the total score by the scorekeeper. The poem/performance will lose .5 (point 5) off of their score for each 10 seconds they go over.

rubrics_metrics.name: No props, costumes, pre-recorded music, or instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet may not use props, costumes, pre-recorded/taped music, or musical instruments while performing. It’s just you and the mic on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: singing, beatboxing, or making other sounds with your body. Examples/anti-patterns: don't use your phone during a performance even if the poem references it; don't point to a toque as a prop; changing clothes during a bout is prohibited and may be considered a costume change. (Rule 4 and 4B)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited abusive/hate content
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem may NOT include sexist, racist, homophobic, or transphobic comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common sense and 'don’t be a jerk' — anger, upset and frustration are allowed emotions to express, but avoid hateful content aimed at protected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging selection and score aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet receives scores out of 10 from five randomly selected judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The high and low scores are dropped and the middle three are added together, giving the poet a total score out of 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-break procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a tie, the top two poets face off in a final round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie resolution is a head-to-head performance between the tied poets to determine placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience interaction: heckling judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The crowd may heckle the judges if they don’t agree with the scores a poet receives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience expression toward judges is explicitly permitted in the rules; no further restrictions provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant commitment to freedom of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: As a participant, I agree to revel in an environment in which freedom of speech, self-determination, and pursuit of creative excellence are inalienable rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms event values around free expression and creative pursuit as part of participant expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sportsmanship and non-violence
rubrics_metrics.description: As a participant, I agree to participate in a way that encourages, illuminates and supports established standards of good sportsmanship and to refuse to allow the competitive challenge of the slam to lead me to violence, interference, or direct threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must allow all others to pursue their craft peacefully and without censure, regardless of present associations or past personal history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance (civil rights/harassment)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a participant, I agree to comply with local, provincial and federal laws pertaining to individual civil rights and physical or sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers must obey applicable laws; legal standards supersede event-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule compliance and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: As a participant, I agree to abide by competition rules, knowing that the consequences for breaking the rules exist and are upheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties will be determined by the severity of the infraction, and the ruling of the presiding emcee and, where applicable, the presiding protest committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, integrity, and demeanor
rubrics_metrics.description: As a participant, I agree to be a fair poet, one who in competition is fair and generous, one who in any connection has recourse to nothing illegitimate; a poet who in defeat demonstrates grace and in victory magnanimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation of ethical behavior, graciousness in loss, and humility in winning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poem quality (Poem — 4 points possible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem is well crafted and demonstrates effective use of poetic language, which may include figurative language and/or rich vocabulary; the poem clearly conveys an idea and a point of view; the poem captures and conveys human emotion and experience; the poem effectively uses rhythm and sound of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category (4 points) assesses craft: language choice, clarity of idea/viewpoint, emotional resonance, and use of rhythm/sound. Judges should weigh these elements when assigning the Poem subscore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation (2 points possible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet’s body movements, facial expressions, and gestures are consistent with and enhance the ideas and mood of the poem; the poet conveys energy and emotion that is consistent with and enhances the ideas and mood of the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category (2 points) evaluates how physicality and emotional energy interpret and reinforce the poem's content/mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance (4 points possible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet speaks clearly; the poet projects their voice; the poet has memorized their poem; the poet effectively performs for the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category (4 points) covers vocal technique, projection, memorization, and overall stage effectiveness.
